questions.question: For mrope_angles(MRoPEConfig(48,16,16,16), t=12, h=0, w=0), what are the first rotation angles for the three bands?
options: [12, 0, 0] for temporal, height, and width
[0, 12, 12], because images use spatial positions first
[1, 1, 1], because the base normalizes every position
[12, 12, 12], because all axes share the temporal coordinate
questions.explanation: For the first pair i=0, theta=base^0=1. The temporal position is 12 and both spatial positions are zero, yielding [12,0,0].

questions.question: Why does M-RoPE carry separate temporal, height, and width positions for a video patch?
options: It removes all positional information so attention is permutation-invariant
It lets the model distinguish time from the two spatial coordinates without a fixed 1D image table
It assigns every video token the same timestamp and only rotates height
It replaces the MLP projector with a Q-Former
questions.explanation: mrope_rotate applies independent rotations to the temporal, height, and width bands. A token can therefore encode frame time and 2D location simultaneously.

questions.question: What FPS does VideoPlan(30s, 81 tokens/frame, 32768 budget, motion='high') choose?
options: 0.25 FPS, because high motion is downsampled most aggressively
4 FPS, because the cap is always four
8 FPS, the highest high-motion candidate under the 13.49 FPS budget ceiling
30 FPS, because one frame is allocated per second of video
questions.explanation: The maximum feasible rate is 32768/(30*81) ≈ 13.49 FPS. The high-motion candidates are [8,4,2,1,...], so 8 FPS is selected.

questions.question: What does parse_tool_call do with text surrounding a valid JSON object?
options: It rejects the whole string because the first character is not '{'
It returns the surrounding prose and discards the object
It converts the object into a Python list of coordinate pairs
It extracts the substring from the first '{' to the last '}' and parses that object
questions.explanation: After a direct json.loads failure, the fallback finds the first and last braces and tries json.loads on that slice. Only if that also fails does it return PARSE_ERROR.

questions.question: What does parse_tool_call return for the malformed string '{"tool": "type_text", "text": "hello"'?
options: A dictionary with tool='PARSE_ERROR' and the original raw string
The completed type_text call with an implicit closing brace
An empty dictionary because malformed JSON is ignored
A list containing the text value only
questions.explanation: The input has no closing brace, so the fallback cannot extract a valid object. parse_tool_call returns {tool: 'PARSE_ERROR', raw: raw}.

questions.question: Which upgrade belongs to Qwen2-VL in the lineage summary?
options: 448px grounding with a Q-Former, before native resolution
M-RoPE, native resolution, and an MLP projector
Dynamic FPS and absolute-time JSON tools, introduced in Qwen2.5-VL
Qwen3 thinking mode and OCR scale
questions.explanation: The summary assigns 2024 Qwen2-VL M-RoPE, native resolution, and an MLP projector. Qwen2.5-VL adds dynamic FPS, absolute time, and JSON agent mode.
